description:
**Record ticket for the Survey spikes. Don't dispatch or plan this ticket.**

The Survey is a read-only look before a task starts. It asks "why is this difficult?", names where the change will bind, and offers a sized menu (just drill / small complete tidy / consolidate the decision / Theseus the area). Plan: `docs/plans/survey.md`; prompt and log: `docs/plans/survey/` (branch `claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j`).

Survey runs post their output here as comments, one per run, each headed `## Survey vN: <ticket> @ <commit>`. The comparison against what actually happened lives in `docs/plans/survey/log.md`.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4151 @ 172f644a1

**Why it's harder than "sort before the split"**

1. **The data for "ready" isn't there.** `splitProjectRoots(tree, shown, waiting)` (`lib/home-view.js:241`) sees only the tree. Readiness in `upNextOf` comes from `buildBlockingGraph(orderedCards)` (:415), and `splitProjectRoots` doesn't get `orderedCards`. It also has a second caller: `homeRowsFor` (`lib/home-rows.js:156`) calls it directly, outside `buildHomeView`. Both callers need the same ranking inputs, or the page's first 3 and the `up-next` fold will disagree, and a task will be shown twice or not at all.

2. **"Ready only" can't filter here; it has to sort.** Home's Up next can drop blocked tasks because they still appear somewhere else. On `/backlog` this list plus its fold is the only place a project's Todo roots appear. Dropping blocked roots would break `tests/unit/lin-4117-reachability-property.test.js` (each open task placed exactly once, paging `backlog` and `up-next` to the end). The same goes for "one per epic": the roots are already a project's top-level items, and only cross-project parents (LIN-4145) share an epic, so capping would only hide tasks. My read: rank ready roots first, then blocked ones, using the same keys, with no epic cap.

3. **It ranks roots, not leaves.** A parent is placed by its own priority, whatever its children's are. The PR should say so. Custom-state roots also count toward `UP_NEXT_PER_PROJECT` (:249–253), so a sort has to keep them visible.

4. **The "keep existing behaviour" bullet is easy to misread.** The list excludes only In Progress and Waiting. Home's Up next tasks *do* appear on `/backlog`, and ranking will put Home's top 5 at the head of their project lists. Keep that; an exclusion would change what can be reached.

5. **The page doesn't say "Up next".** The section has no heading, only a "show N more" fold. "Up next" is just in names (`kind: up-next`, `home-fold-up-next`, llms.txt :72). Renaming costs almost nothing, so the real decision is the order.

6. **The existing tests won't catch it either way.** The fixtures in `lin-4024-home-view` (:115) and `lin-4024-home-rows` (:87) use `priority: 0` and no `createdAt`. Every ranking key ties, so the order falls back to tree position, and those tests will probably pass unchanged. A green suite proves nothing about the new order.

**Baseline:** at 172f644a1, `lin-4024-home-rows`, `lin-4024-home-view`, `lin-4113-home-desk`, `lin-4117-reachability-property`, `lin-4139-up-next-ranking` and `lin-4120-home-backlog` pass, 113/113.

**What I'd do first**

Write the failing witness before touching code. Give a project a Low Todo root first and a High Todo root fourth. Assert that High is in `view.trees[0].incomplete` and that the `up-next` fold doesn't return it. Run the lin-4117 property alongside it.

Then make one change where the two callers meet. Pull the comparator out of `upNextOf`. Build the rank context (inDegree, positionOf) once, in a helper that `buildHomeView` and `homeRowsFor` both call, and pass it into `splitProjectRoots`. Don't give each caller its own sort.

## Survey global (code only): LIN-4151 @ 172f644a1

**1. Where it lands.** `lib/home-view.js` `splitProjectRoots` (:241), a 15-line tree-order loop. Its two callers each work out the split themselves: `buildHomeView` (:518) keeps three roots plus a count, and `homeRowsFor` (`home-rows.js:156-158`) rebuilds the view, then splits again to page the fold. The module is dense, closely documented and moving fast (six tickets in weeks). Each change made the page and its folds agree more, but each added a set (`shown`, `waiting`, `linked`, `onHome`) that every placement has to thread through. The ranking in `upNextOf` (:412) is private and mixed into eligibility (card pool, seeds, decided state, blocking, epic cap). Since LIN-4120, Home draws no project sections, so `upNext`, `UP_NEXT_PER_PROJECT` and `kind: 'up-next'` name a list only `/backlog` draws. That page never shows the words "Up next": its fold reads "show N more" (`render.js:505`). The name lives only in identifiers, the module header (:11) and `llms.txt:72`, so renaming is cheap and changes no DOM.

**2. Done the obvious way** (pull out the comparator, sort before the split):
- **Readiness has no input.** `splitProjectRoots` never sees `orderedCards`, so "ready only" adds a parameter at both call sites. If one drifts, page and fold disagree.
- **Blocked roots need a home.** If they're dropped from the three, they have to rank after the ready ones in the fold, or they vanish from `/backlog`.
- **Custom-state roots** count toward the three and always stay visible (:252). Ranked or pinned? Decide.
- **One per epic means nothing here.** Each row is a root with its subtree, so it is its own epic (LIN-4145 cross-project roots aside). Leave the cap out.
- **Second copy.** `compareKeys`, `timeOr` and the keys (`priority || 5`, due, created) get copied unless they're exported as one thing. Position is the root's index in `openNodesOf`'s output.
- **Tests won't notice.** The pinned fixtures (`lin-4024-home-view.test.js:125`, `lin-4024-home-rows.test.js:93`) have equal priority and no dates, so they pass ranked or not. The task needs its own witnesses. Baseline: six home/backlog suites, 117/117 pass. No test ties `llms.txt`'s fold wording to `render.js`.
- **The acceptance is wrong about dedupe.** The project list dedupes only against Running and `waiting`, not Home's Up next. A task can sit in both today.

**3. Better, within cost:** one exported ranking (keys plus comparator) for `upNextOf` and the split. `buildHomeView` returns each project's `upNextRest` and `homeRowsFor` pages it instead of re-splitting: one derivation for page and fold. Update the header and `llms.txt:72`/`:123`.

**Better still, not this task's:** separate `upNextOf`'s eligibility from its ranking, as a candidate model both lists filter. Split the 576-line `home-view.js` (Running, project split, Up next, recent, Waiting). Rename the Home-era identifiers and the "Home's folds" comments in `render.js` that now describe `/backlog`.

## Survey global (code only): LIN-4048 @ 13fe24a04

**The headline: at 13fe24a04 the bug as written is already fixed.** The code has moved past the ticket's anchors. `mainActionOf` no longer exists. LIN-4071 (27ae64ad) and LIN-4104 (4a0d90ee) moved the decision to the server, which is the ticket's own first "unvalidated idea". `buildRowStates` (`lib/task-page-loader.js:1154`) sets `action: finished ? NO_RUN_ACTION : …`. The task page's `/state` takes the gather's action (`routes/task-page.js` `sessionsOfState`), and so does its page-load row record (`rowRecordOf({ decided: taskState })`). The `task` surface has `sharedButtons: true`, so `renderGo` takes the `runOfferOf` branch, and for `kind: 'none'` it draws nothing. I checked this with a scratch vm-sandbox probe: a real `/state` body for a Done leaf returns `{"kind":"none"}`, and the task page renders **no** Go, Run to PR, Next step or Run to Done. An incomplete held set (action null) also renders no button. An unfinished leaf still renders all three rungs. `tests/unit/lin-4042-finished-no-run-to-pr.test.js` already has a `surface: 'task'` finished case, and it passes (15/15). A test that "fails before the change" can't be written against the main button.

**1. Where it lands, and how that part is doing.** It lands in `public/prompt-section.js` (2,874 lines) and its `caps` table. The trend is good: decisions are leaving the browser (`row.finished` was removed, and `takesNoRun`/`runOfferOf` read one server offer). The one leftover asymmetry is in `renderRunBlock`. Home has an early return for a finished task with nothing running. The `!caps.runBox` branch, used by the task page and Swipe, has none. So on a Done task page the probe still paints `opened-task-runs-on`, `run-on-what` and **`run-change`**: a "runs on … / Change" line for a run that cannot happen. Also, if the quota is known, renderGo still prints "N of M runs left today" beside no button.

**2. Done the obvious way.** The obvious way is to have the task page read `finished` the way Home once did. That would bring back a browser-side tracker guard that LIN-4071 removed on purpose: two owners for one decision, and it would contradict the header comment of the 4042 test file. Nothing would catch the duplicate. If the task is redone as "add a server field", it would duplicate `NO_RUN_ACTION`. Neither one is needed.

**3. What would leave it better, at this task's cost.** Close the main-button acceptance as already covered by LIN-4071/4104, and spend the task on the leftover asymmetry instead. Give the `!caps.runBox` branch the same `!active && takesNoRun` shape as Home: drop runs-on, Change and the step line, and keep `renderRunMore` and the proposals. Hide the quota span when `takesNoRun`. Add one task-surface test asserting no `run-change` or `opened-task-runs-on` on a Done body. That test fails today, so the acceptance criterion holds. Running and queued boxes are not affected because `active` gates the branch. **Better still, but not this task's to carry:** fold the task page's run block into Home's (`runBox`). The `caps` table keeps growing flags to hide the split. LIN-4040's three-button rework is where that belongs.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4048 @ 13fe24a04

**Short version: at 13fe24a04 the reported symptom looks already fixed, so the hard part is that the ticket describes code that no longer exists.**

**What the ground looks like**

- `mainActionOf` is gone from `lib/task-state.js`. LIN-4104 D1 (#2225) replaced it with `runOfferOf`. `buildRowStates` (`lib/task-page-loader.js:1149-1154`) sets `action: finished ? NO_RUN_ACTION : …` from the held set's tracker type, and `/state` forwards it (`routes/task-page.js` `sessionsOfState`).
- `row.finished` is gone too. LIN-4071 (#2222) removed the browser's tracker-word guard, and `rowRecordOf` now carries only `action`.
- `renderGo` on the `task` surface (`sharedButtons: true`) draws the rungs only when `runOfferOf(state, opts).kind === 'offer'` (`public/prompt-section.js:317-325`). For `none` it draws nothing.
- On page load, `renderTaskRunControl` (`lib/render-task-page.js:821`) returns `''` when `model.finished`, so a Done task's page has no run control at all. `tests/unit/lin-3975-task-run-control.test.js:339` pins this.
- I probed the real `/state` route through `tests/fixtures/state-route.js`:

  | Task | `action` | `busy` |
  |---|---|---|
  | Completed leaf | `{kind:'none'}` | `false` |
  | Canceled leaf | `{kind:'none'}` | `false` |
  | Completed leaf with a failed stage | `{kind:'none'}` | `false` |
  | Started leaf | `offer` | `false` |
- `tests/unit/lin-4042-finished-no-run-to-pr.test.js` already has "task page: a finished task (action.kind none) … offers no stage step and no Go" (in the LIN-4071 block). It passes at 13fe24a04.

So acceptance item 1 holds today, and no red test can be written against it.

**What might still be real: acceptance item 2, which now fails the other way round**

Because the page-load mount is skipped for a finished task, a Done task with a run still **running or queued** gets no run control on its task page. That means no running box and no Stop / Undo. Home keeps them (the `!active` early return in `renderRunBlock`). Whether this matters depends on whether a task can be Done while a run is still held. A close-out run that marks the task Done mid-run is the obvious case.

**What I'd do first**

1. Confirm that the ticket was written before #2222, #2225 and #2257 landed, and close the reported symptom as covered by LIN-4071 and LIN-4104.
2. Decide whether "Done + running → Stop on the task page" is wanted. If it is, it's a separate small change: mount the control when `model.finished` but a session is held, and let `/state`'s `none` plus the active run paint the running box. The red test would be a `page(model({ finished: true, …running }))` render in the lin-3975 suite that expects the mount, plus a `surface: 'task'` vm render in prompt-section. One trap: the `!caps.runBox` branch of `renderRunBlock` has no `takesNoRun` early return and relies on `renderGo` alone, so check that it still draws the running line and Stop when `action` is `none`.
3. Don't add a browser-side `finished` read again. LIN-4071 removed it on purpose ("no surface reads the tracker's word").

## Survey global (code only): LIN-4143 @ c70b004c0

**Where it lands.** `lib/task-page-loader.js` (1,535 lines), which makes two unguarded ruling reads: `rulingFor` (:1271, which feeds the model and the question card) and `gatheredStateOf` (:1422, which feeds the state pill through `gatherTaskStates`). This part of the code is getting better. LIN-4024 made `lib/ruling-standing.js` the only reader of ruling standing. LIN-4114 moved the predicate into `lib/live-anchor.js` and added `liveGuard` to `readRulingStanding`/`rulingStandingOf`. Home already passes `liveGuard: true` (`lib/home-row-states.js:87`). The task page is the last user of the shared reader that reads without the guard. The `liveGuard = false` default exists only to keep it that way (`lib/unanswered-decisions.js:976`: "Off by default: the task page's read does not change").

Why it matters: without the guard, a mid-turn or indeterminate row gets `effect: null` (the LIN-4242 witness pins this down). `lib/question-card.js:132` then emits `data-effect=""`, and `public/question-cards.js:367` falls back to `'resume'`. The press-time check (`public/common.js:1401`, G1) only downgrades on a *terminal* anchor, not a live one. So the effect the card renders with is the only live-run guard on this surface.

**Done the obvious way.** Add `liveGuard: true` to `rulingFor`. One token, no new home, no second copy. The guard only changes `effect`; `openLoopIds` is built before effects are resolved, so `waitingFor` and the pill don't move. Things the task should know:
- Pass it in `gatheredStateOf` too. That changes no behaviour, but it keeps a single page load from reading the standing two ways.
- Liveness scope: the feed scans the workspace's `merged` set. The task page scans only this task's own loops, filtered to the 30-day window. For a row anchored on this task that's the right set. One difference: a run still live but dispatched more than 30 days ago is filtered out here.
- What has to learn about it: three comments will go stale. They are the consumer list in `lib/live-anchor.js`'s header, the "off by default" comment above, and the `readRulingStanding` doc. Nothing would flag them. The witness needs a loader-level test (task with a live run and an open ruling → card row `effect: 'record'`). `tests/unit/task-page-question.test.js` is the nearest home. No test currently pins the unguarded task-page behaviour, so nothing will break loudly. Without the new test, a slide back wouldn't be caught either.

**Better, at this task's cost.** After the change, every `readRulingStanding` caller passes `true`. The task could remove the parameter instead of adding a third `true`: make the guard unconditional in `rulingStandingOf` whenever no `liveDispatchOnAnchor` is injected. Then there's one way to read standing, not a flag to forget. The remaining callers are just `buildRowStates`'s fallback (`lib/task-page-loader.js:1131`, used when there's no `ruling`). The fallback would gain the guard as well, which looks right. The other update is the LIN-4242 foil test (`liveGuard: false`, :280), which would need to compare against the raw `collectUnansweredDecisions` instead. Small, and inside this task's files.

**Better still, not this task's.**
- `routes/proxy-rulings.js:247` writes its own copy of the predicate instead of calling `liveOnAnchor`. Its own comment names this disagreement class as an earlier incident.
- `routes/dashboard-session-state.js:250` keeps a re-export shim for `liveOnAnchor`.
- The client's `effect || 'resume'` default fails open. A missing effect should probably mean record. That's a separate change in behaviour.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4143 @ c70b004c0

**Why it's difficult: the premise looks wrong at this commit, so the witness may already pass.**

The task page's question card doesn't read `readRulingStanding`'s rows. In `lib/task-page-loader.js`:

- The card is `model.question` from `buildQuestion` (`:565`). Its rows come from `deriveSessionDecisions(enriched, { now })` (`:571`). That is the run page's reader, and it always passes `liveDispatchOnAnchor: liveOnAnchor(livenessScope)` (`routes/dashboard-session-state.js:244`), scoped to the task's own loops. So the card's `data-effect` is already guarded.
- The unguarded standing (`rulingFor`, `:1273`; `gatheredStateOf`, `:1422`) feeds only two things: `openLoopIds` → `waitingFor`, which decides whether the card shows (`render-task-page.js:790`), and `gatherTaskStates`. Neither reads `row.effect`, and I found no `effect` read in the row-state code. The ticket's line refs (`:1236`, `:1385`) are about 37 lines stale.

I probed `buildTaskPageModel` at c70b004c0 and compared it with the feed's reduction:

| scenario | feed | unguarded standing | task-page card |
|---|---|---|---|
| waiting ruling + live sibling run | resumable/resume | resume | shown, `resume` |
| gone ruling + live sibling | gone/**record** | **dispatch** | not shown (no waiting session) |
| mid-turn ruling | **record** | **null** | not shown |

The guard only changes the effect for `gone` and `mid-turn` rows. The card only shows while a session is waiting, and the waiting loop is `resumable`. Branch 1 of `resolveEffect` returns `resume` for that before the guard runs (`unanswered-decisions.js:154-165`). So the witness ("live run + open ruling → card `effect: 'record'`") seems impossible to build on this page, and wherever the card does show, it already matches the feed. A test written to the witness would pass before any change, or would need fixtures the real flow never produces.

**Smaller real differences worth naming:**
- Liveness scope. The task page's `enriched` is horizon `'all'` and unwindowed; the feed's `merged` is the workspace set. A stuck non-terminal loop older than 30 days counts as live on the task page and not in the feed.
- `public/question-cards.js:367` defaults an empty `data-effect` to `'resume'`. `deliveredEffect` (`common.js:1456`) then turns that into `dispatch` for any non-resumable disposition. An unguarded `mid-turn` row (effect `null`) would therefore start a run if it ever reached a card. The press-time check in `deliverRulingDispatch` (`common.js:1401`) only checks for a terminal tracker state, not a live run. That is the real collision path. It's latent here, but any surface that renders unguarded standing rows is exposed.

**What I'd do first:**
1. Write the witness as a unit test against `buildTaskPageModel` + `renderTaskPage`, assert on the card's `data-effect` and run it at c70b004c0 first. If it passes (I expect so), take that back to the ticket rather than ship a no-op.
2. If a change is still wanted, it's cheap: pass `liveGuard: true` at both `readRulingStanding` sites. Only `effect` changes, and nothing on this page reads it, so LIN-4114's feared behaviour change seems not to exist. But that is consistency, not a fix. The more useful fix is failing closed in the client: treat an empty `data-effect` as `record`, not `resume`.

Baseline: `lin-4114-home-waiting` + `lin-4242-waiting-live` unit tests pass, 28/28.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4248 @ 2eb73ae07

**Why it will be difficult**

The copy is easy: `place-change.mjs` imports only Node builtins and `scripts/code-shape/seams.mjs`, which is on main, and `handoff-place-concept.md` is not on main yet, so it goes too. The templates are the hard part, for three reasons.

1. **Nothing can supply the base commit yet.** The prompt must name main's head at dispatch, but `generatePrompt` is synchronous and network-free (`lib/prompt-templates.js:251-279`). Dispatch passes it only issue, parent, siblings, project, children, comments and attachments (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1549`). The checkout lives on the runner, which receives only a repo name (`resolveRepo`, `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs:243`). Nothing on the server reads a branch head today. That leaves two choices. Dispatch could learn to fetch the SHA (a new GitHub call, a token and a project-to-repo mapping), which is arguably outside "no other behaviour changes". Or the template tells the session to resolve `origin/main` itself and name it in the heading, which changes the tuned wording.

2. **"Wording unchanged" runs into the stage frame.** `finishStagePrompt` wraps every body. It adds Scope and Authority, which every template must carry (`tests/unit/recommend-stage-assembly.test.js:115`), then the stage contract, grounding notes and attachments, and finally the dispatch preamble ("mandate … open PRs … END with PR link, commit SHA", `lib/proxy-preamble.js`). The hand runs survived the preamble. The grounding is the trap. A kind missing from `GROUNDING_BY_KIND` (`lib/prompt-formatters.js:610`) gets all four notes, including "re-read that source at HEAD" and the close-out and fix notes. Those contradict "don't look at anything after {BASE}" and "read-only", and no test fails if the kind is left out. The Survey kinds need `[]`, as triage has.

3. **"Never offered on its own" is two decisions in two places.** Leaving out `route` keeps a kind out of the stage selector (`getSelectableStages`). But the run box's "Another step" list reads only `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION` (`lib/task-page-loader.js:1022`), and so does the router's refusal. Retro is in both. The new kinds must be in both, and the Done-when proof should check both.

Then there is the list of registries, nearly all enforced by tests that say how to fix them: source and rendered ceilings plus `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` (`prompt-size-budget.test.js:297`), `BUCKET_OF_KIND`, `STAGE_INTENT`, `COMPLETION_SIGNALS`, `STAGE_LEADS` (if `goal()` is used), the template count in `public/llms.txt` and `docs/architecture/source-map.md` (17 today), the run-view labels and the session-fit map in `prompt-templates.test.js`.

Smaller frictions:
- `{RECORD}` folds into `{TICKET}`.
- The global prompt hard-codes `LIN-4150` and has a title line above its `---`.
- open-0 sits inside `prompt.md`'s prose. Once the notebook is on main, the doc and the template are two copies by design. "Unchanged" needs a test that pulls the text from the doc, or they will drift.

**What I'd do first**

Settle the base question (the server resolves the SHA, or the session does) and write the fill-in contract: each brace, and where its value comes from. Then build open-0 alone through `generatePrompt`, render it for a real ticket, and diff that against a hand-sent prompt. The diff shows what the frame adds and what has to be turned off. Then add the second.

## Survey global (code only): LIN-4248 @ 2eb73ae07

**Where it lands.** `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` (1,160 lines, 17 templates) and `lib/prompt-templates.js`. Since LIN-3299/3300 this part has been tidying up: one routing path, `getSelectableStages()` as the only list of options, and "no `route` means never offered" (that's how `retro` is kept out). The cost: a template is now a row in roughly nine parallel per-kind tables, most of them checked against `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` keys by tests.

**Done the obvious way** (two `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` entries with no `route`), these would have to learn about it:
- Tests catch a miss in: `STAGE_LEADS` and the `## Goal`/`## Process` body shape; `STAGE_INTENT`; `GROUNDING_BY_KIND` (an unlisted kind gets every note, including "implement the fix"); `BUCKET_OF_KIND`; `COMPLETION_SIGNALS`; the rendered and source ceilings plus `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES`; and the template counts in `source-map.md`, `executive-summary.md` and `landing.md`.
- Nothing catches a miss in: `run-view.js` labels, the `workflow-config.js` enum, `llm-jobs.js`, or the row owed to `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`.
- `executive-summary.md:151` says "17 prompt templates with `route`", but only 16 have one. The count test keeps that number tied to the key count, so it will read 19 and stay wrong.

**Where "unchanged wording" collides with the template shape.**
- `finishStagePrompt` adds a Scope and Authority section, grounding and attachments to every template. The lead test also forces a Goal/Process split that neither prompt has.
- `generate()` is synchronous and makes no network calls. Nothing in the prompt context knows main's head. Fetching it at dispatch would be new behaviour. Telling the session to resolve `origin/main` and name it in the heading is cheaper, at the cost of one wording change.
- Both prompts become a second copy. The notebook's `prompt.md` and `global-offshoot-prompt-v2-code.md` land on main carrying the same text, so doc and template can drift silently.
- The name "survey" is already taken: about 200 `scripts/survey-*.mjs` files belong to a separate research programme.

**A routing gap.** `parseRouteDecision` refuses only `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION` (`retro`), not kinds that lack a `route`. A selector reply naming the new stage would be accepted though never offered. `recommend-stage-assembly.test.js` builds `ROUTABLE` from that same set, so its routed arm would treat the new kinds as routable.

**Better, at this task's cost:**
- Add both keys to `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`, so the refusal is real and the routed tests skip them. The byte-pinned `tests/fixtures/stage-router-prompts/` staying identical is the cheap proof that routing didn't change.
- Fix the `executive-summary` wording to "N prompt templates (M with `route`)".
- Use keys that won't collide (`survey-task` / `survey-place`).
- Put the prompt text in one place. Either the template reads the moved doc at HEAD, the way `lib/prompts/worker-lane-kickoff.js` serves `docs/worker-lane-prompt.md`, or the doc names the template as its source. Not both as live copies.
- If the Goal/Process split is forced, record what was wrapped.

**Better still, not this task's:**
- Derive "excluded" from a missing `route`, so there is one source.
- Fold the nine per-kind tables into the template definition, so a new template is one object.
- Consider whether read-only forecasts that post one comment belong in the stage registry at all, or in the docs-backed, non-registered prompt pattern that `lib/prompts/` already has.
